Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team here is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Procurement asked us to push back on the pricing appendix: we've attached a redline (Ellipsis_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf) proposing a "Bandwidth Protection" clause under Exhibit B. The core ask is twofold:

- When monthly consumption drops below 60% of committed throughput for two consecutive months, a temporary surcharge of 10% on per-token rates applies to recover idle capacity costs (we show the math in the attached spreadsheet).
- We want a hard floor (no more than a 5% permanent reduction in committed rate) to avoid long-term rate erosion.

This is pretty standard for our other vendors, but we want to confirm Redwood's flexibility here and get legal comments on the proposed wording. We marked inline suggestions in the PDF.

Can you please loop in the right folks and let us know if Redwood can accept a surcharge-based stabilization (vs. immediate contract true-ups)? We'd prefer to avoid a mid-term re-commit if possible.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30-min call if that's easier.

Best,

Maya — thanks for the ping. A couple quick commercial notes:

- Ellipsis is mid-market but growing quickly; they're asking for a protection construct we've seen before. Sales prefers a surcharge over an immediate permanent true-up if it helps close and preserves relationship momentum.
- We should tie surcharge triggers to a clear measurement (monthly active token consumption vs. committed throughput) and allow them to cure (e.g., two consecutive months triggers, but they can cure within one month to avoid surcharge).
- Surcharge cap: propose 10% per month, max of 3 months in any rolling 12 month period. After 3 surcharge months, we can require a commercial review (not automatic contract reprice).
- Hard floor concern: we should not promise anything that limits our future pricing flexibility. Instead, propose language that limits permanent reductions to "no more than 5% below the most recent true-up-adjusted committed rate without mutual written agreement." That preserves a bilateral negotiation.

I'll defer to Marcus for legal wording but happy to have Sales present this as a commercial concession. Let me know if you want me to lead the call with Ellipsis next week.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Suggested contract language — bandwidth protection / surcharge (track changes inline)

Folks — below is a concise alternative that addresses Ellipsis's commercial concern while protecting Redwood. I'm pasting proposed language you can drop into Exhibit B. If you want a version with embedded tracked changes, see the Maya_response_track_changes.docx I put in the thread.

PROPOSED: Bandwidth Protection and Stabilization.
1) Definitions: "Committed Throughput" means the average monthly token throughput agreed in the Order Form for the applicable Billing Period. "Measured Consumption" means Customer's measured average monthly token throughput as reported by Redwood's usage logs.
2) Trigger: If Measured Consumption is less than sixty percent (60%) of Committed Throughput for two (2) consecutive Billing Periods, Redwood may, upon notice, apply a temporary Production Surcharge equal to ten percent (10%) of the per-token rates in effect for the impacted Billing Periods.
3) Limitations: The Production Surcharge shall not be applied for more than three (3) Billing Periods in any rolling twelve (12) Billing Period window. Application of the Production Surcharge does not constitute an automatic permanent repricing.
4) Cure; Mitigation: Prior to any surcharge assessment, Customer shall have a ten (10) Business Day cure period to demonstrate recovery in consumption. Redwood may offer alternative mitigation credits or temporary burst credits at its discretion in lieu of surcharge.
5) Permanent Reductions: Any proposal to permanently reduce Committed Throughput by an amount exceeding five percent (5%) of the most recently adjusted Committed Throughput shall require mutual written agreement and, if requested by Redwood, a commercial review to assess impact on capacity planning.
6) Audit and Measurement: Measurements shall be taken from Redwood's usage logs. Customer may request one audit per 12-month period; any audit showing material measurement error (>2%) shall be mutually reconciled.

Notes: - I tightened the cure window and added an audit clause to prevent disputes. - We should avoid hard language that locks in floors forever; clause 5 requires mutual agreement which should satisfy their ask while protecting us.

If Sales is comfortable, I can put this into a tracked PDF and return to Ellipsis with a short summary paragraph.

Marcus
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Lara / Tom,

Appreciate the clear redlines and worked example — helpful. We've reviewed internally and propose the following compromise (Marcus pasted the key legal language below for reference). Summary of the offer: 

- Trigger: 2 consecutive months <60% of committed throughput triggers a temporary Production Surcharge.
- Surcharge: 10% per-token, capped at 3 months in any rolling 12 months.
- Cure: 10 Business Day cure window before surcharge is charged; Redwood may offer credits or burst credits instead of surcharge.
- Permanent reductions: We will not accept an automatic permanent cut; any reduction exceeding 5% of the most recent adjusted commitment will require mutual written agreement and a commercial review.

We've attached a tracked PDF that contains Marcus's exact proposed wording and a short annex showing the surcharge math using Ellipsis's numbers. Can you review and confirm if this aligns with your stakeholders? If yes, we can prepare a DocuSign packet and schedule a 30-minute call to finalize.

If you prefer immediate language edits, Marcus can provide a redline that accepts minor drafting tweaks your counsel requests.

Thanks — speaking for the team, we want to keep this simple and mutually fair so we can move to signature.

Best regards,
Maya Srinivasan
